title: Quantization NaN debug scratchpad (INT8/FP8/BF16)
content:
Context:
- Reproducing intermittent NaNs in generation when using INT8/FP8 quantized weights on the 7B family. Happens more often on longer sequences (>512) but not strictly correlated to length.
- Baseline BF16 full-precision run is clean. INT8/FP8 runs sometimes produce NaN tokens mid-generation and crash runtime.

Observed behaviour (notes + snippets):
- Minimal reproduction command (local dev machine):
  python -m torchrun --nproc_per_node=1 tools/generate.py \
    --model checkpoints/7b-qint8 --quantize int8 --seq_len 1024 --batch_size 1 \
    --prompt-file tests/long_prompt.txt

- Example runtime output around failure:
  === BEGIN LOG ===
  token 342: generated token id 5021 -> logit inf
  RuntimeError: value cannot be converted to finite floating point (got inf)
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "tools/generate.py", line 214, in <module>
      outputs = model.generate(inputs)
    File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1190, in __call__
      return forward_call(*input, **kwargs)
  ...
  === END LOG ===

- Another run with full debug prints on matmul shows some rows with huge values before softmax. Suspect out-of-range activations.

Commands tried / quick experiments:
- Re-run with different quantization backends:
  QUANT_BACKEND=fbgemm python -m ... --quantize int8  # no improvement
  QUANT_BACKEND=fx2trt python -m ... --quantize int8  # occasionally different failure point
- Force BF16 activation casts before attention matmul:
  patched attention: q = q.to(torch.bfloat16); k = k.to(torch.bfloat16) -> reduces frequency of NaN but not eliminated.
- Disable fused kernels (to narrow down source):
  export DISABLE_FUSED_KERNS=1; python -m ... --quantize int8 -> still see NaNs but different stack.
- Per-channel vs per-tensor quantization test:
  quantize --per_channel true -> slightly better stability (fewer NaNs).
- Calibration dataset size scaling: small cal set (100 samples) vs larger (2k) changed distribution; larger cal improved stability in some runs.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Activation overflow due to scale mismatch between weight quantization and activation dynamic range (INT8/FP8 scales too small -> matmul produces large vals).
2) LayerNorm / RMSNorm quantization is lossy and causes occasional divide-by-zero or extreme scaling when epsilon handling differs across kernels.
3) KV-cache reuse + quantization rounding accumulates error across many past tokens -> grows magnitude and triggers NaN.
4) Fused attention kernel bug for certain sequence lengths / batch shapes when using mixed FP8/INT8 pathway.
5) Per-tensor quantization not capturing per-channel variance in older linear layers -> single bad channel saturates.

Evidence / supporting notes:
- Per-channel quant seems to reduce rate of NaN (supports #5).
- Casting activations to BF16 before matmul reduces frequency (supports #1/#2).
- NaNs more common after cache length > 256 tokens (supports #3).
- Different quant backends fail at different points (points to backend-specific fused kernel bug for some runs)

Immediate next steps / experiments to run (short):
- Add per-layer debug dump that logs max/min/std of Q/K/V activations and weight scales every forward pass (write to local tmp) to pinpoint which layer explodes.
- Re-run with disabled KV-cache to test hypothesis #3: --disable-kv-cache flag.
- Run with deterministic RNG and seed to try to reproduce consistently: torch.manual_seed(42); set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.
- Try strict BF16-only path for attention: force activation casts and remove INT8 path to see if NaN disappears.
- Add clipping of activations before softmax: torch.clamp(x, -1e4, 1e4) as a temporary mitigant.

Longer experiments / infra work:
- Build instrumented model with hooks logging layernorm eps values and whether any zeros in denominator.
- Add unit test that generates long sequence and asserts no NaN for 100 seeds.
- Create small canary on Dedicated infra to check if hardware (A100 vs H100) affects rate.

Notes on potential fixes to try if hypothesis confirmed:
- Use per-channel scales for problematic linear layers; tighten calibration procedure (percentile range instead of min/max).
- Adjust quantization zero_point handling for int8 symmetric/asymmetric mismatch.
- Increase layernorm epsilon in FP8/INT8 codepaths to avoid divide-by-zero.
- Accumulate KV in BF16 while keeping weights INT8 (hybrid approach).

Quick checklist (for me):
- [ ] Add per-layer activation logging hook (priority high).
- [ ] Run --disable-kv-cache reproducer (priority medium).
- [ ] Try per-channel quant globally and compare failure rate across 50 runs (priority high).
- [ ] Open PR with activation clamps as a short-term fix (priority low, discuss w/ runtime team).
- [ ] Sync with Carlos on fused kernel test matrix (priority high).

Scratch console history (most relevant):
- git checkout -b quant/nan-debug
- python -m tools/generate.py --model ckpts/7b-int8 --quantize int8 --seed 42 --seq_len 1024
- python -c "import torch; print(torch.get_default_dtype(), torch.cuda.is_available())"
- QUANT_BACKEND=fbgemm python -m ...

Random observations / hypotheses to keep in mind:
- Some older layers with very small weights (close to zero) may produce large reciprocal scales during calibration -> numerical instability.
- FP8 dynamic range is narrower than expected for rare high-magnitude tokens in long context.
- If scaling steps differ between encoder/decoder style layers we might be mixing incompatible quant params.

Links / refs:
- internal PR with quant util changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123
- similar incident notes from Maya: docs/quantization/quantization-nan-incident-maya-2026-03-09
- ticket: JIRA-QUANT-78 (investigation task)

If I get a solid reproduction (deterministic/seeded), next action is to capture a minimal repro and open a dedicated bug with stack trace + offending layer dump.

-- Lee
